title: The FakeServer is the public demo — and the production Live Viewer binding is still open

decision.summary: The public `herald-demo` is the FakeServer-based sample at `Herald.RestApi.FakeServer/samples/DemoApp` (PackageId Herald.DemoApp, v0.1.0-alpha.1). It serves the JSX SPA, seeds a demo tenant, runs a real Herald.OSS pipeline over synthetic events, and honors the tenant-scoped Live Viewer admin API the SPA depends on. The umbrella `Modules/DemoApp` — which wraps Herald.Server — is NOT the demo: Herald.Server speaks only the legacy flat API, so it 404s on the `/live-viewer` family the SPA calls.
decision.rationale: Two server stacks exist, and they speak different APIs. The JSX SPA was built against the tenant-scoped Live Viewer admin family. Only the FakeServer (and the in-memory reference host) implement that family. Herald.Server, which the umbrella DemoApp wraps, implements the legacy flat API and never registered the tenant-scoped routes — so the umbrella package shows the SPA but 404s the moment it tries to hydrate. The FakeServer sample is the one package that satisfies all four demo promises at once: serves the SPA, seeds a tenant, runs a real pipeline, and answers the API the SPA speaks. Pointing the demo at the reference host was rejected — it is in-memory, has no live pipeline, does not serve the SPA, and carries no seed, so it would show empty or fake data and break the 'watch a live Herald pipeline' promise.

context-matrix.verdict: chosen — satisfies all four demo promises
rejected as the demo — 404s on the /live-viewer family the SPA needs; this is the two-package trap
rejected as the demo — in-memory, no live pipeline, no SPA, no seed; proves the wire shape only

traps-avoided.why: Herald.Server and Herald.RestApi.Host speak DIFFERENT APIs. Herald.Server speaks the legacy flat API; the reference host speaks the tenant-scoped Live Viewer family the SPA depends on. A reader who assumes 'the server is the server' will wire the SPA to the wrong one and watch it 404. The two stacks are not interchangeable.

The umbrella `Modules/DemoApp` (wraps Herald.Server) and the FakeServer sample `samples/DemoApp` (PackageId Herald.DemoApp v0.1.0-alpha.1) can both look like 'the demo'. Only the FakeServer sample is. The umbrella one 404s the SPA. Repacking or publishing the wrong one ships a broken first impression.

traps-avoided.trap: Repointing the demo at the reference host to 'get the right API'
traps-avoided.why: The reference host speaks the right API but has no live pipeline, no SPA, and no seed. Swapping to it trades a 404 for empty data — it defeats the 'watch a real Herald pipeline' promise that is the whole reason the demo exists.

open-work.item: Bind ILiveViewerAdminApi to a real Herald.Server pipeline and host the tenant-scoped family there
open-work.owner: Glenn (D3 scaffold), with Richard architecture review before the larger binding
open-work.notes: The pipeline operations already exist on `HeraldManagementApi` (GetLevelStyles, GetCategoryStyles, GetCustomLevels, SetMinimumLevel, SetFlightRecorderConfig, enricher add/remove). The missing piece is the tenant-scoped routing shell plus the `LiveViewerState` mapping — not the underlying pipeline operations. The route-mapping glue in `LiveViewerAdminEndpoints` is portable; the `InMemoryLiveViewerAdmin` interface impl is portable. Two layered options were sketched: (A) a minimal first-impression fix that implements just GET /live-viewer over the existing HeraldManagementApi getters — clears the error banner, panels hydrate, live logs flow, but style edits and CRUD still 404; (B) the full production binding = #38 = everything in the SPA works, larger, warrants architecture review plus a plan plus code review plus tests.
Orthogonal cleanup. The DemoApp already ships and serves the JSX SPA. The Vue port is a separate, deprecated parallel client. Removing it fixes none of the API-gap issues; it is independent tidy-up.

changes-already-made: Modules/Server/Program.cs: renamed the primary demo pipeline `code-built-pipeline` -> `default` (the OSS dashboard targets the pipeline named `default`). Verified the pipeline registers as default/default and /health returns 200. Correct regardless of how the production binding is resolved.

Repacked the shipped JSX so its default scope is `default`/`default` rather than a stale `acme` artifact baked into an older nupkg build (the current JSX source already defaults to default/default in store-bridge.jsx).
